offerIntro.MainBody:
You market the same platform to aerospace engineers, automotive safety teams, biotech researchers, and quantitative financial analysts. Every single one of them needs a completely different pitch, and that is the part of B2B marketing that has never scaled.

So plug in your data and let agents build a page for each segment, each account, each open deal. In your brand, on your domain, rewritten as the conversation moves. That is Limitless personalization.

It built the page you are reading. Over lunch, we show your team how to do the same.

aboutIntro.MainBody:
Optimizely gives you all the tools you need to create and optimize every digital experience, with AI agents taking on the work about work. One platform, multiple use cases, trusted by 10,000+ brands.

Use-case highlight — Limitless personalization: turn your data into fully personalized pages, on brand and on your domain, that keep rewriting themselves as the account moves. The same logic you apply to building AI for engineers, applied to how your marketing team reaches them.

aboutPillars.Title: Always yours
aboutPillars.Description: MathWorks’s brand, your tone, your messaging guidelines across 17+ industries, your data rules. Loaded in from the start and published to your own subdomain, so every page reads like your team wrote it. In every way that counts, they did.

aboutPillars.Title: Always on
aboutPillars.Description: Pages travel the journey alongside the buyer. An account announces a new defence program, a deal moves stage, a contact opens an email or turns up at MATLAB EXPO — and their page already knows, and says something new.

aboutPillars.Title: Always traceable
aboutPillars.Description: Every block traces back to the signal behind it, so anyone on your team can see why a page says what it says. Nothing publishes until you allow it, and you set that rule per program.

problemThesis.Headline: Seventeen industries. Multiple personas each. Thousands of pages. Four steps.
problemThesis.Body:
Aerospace engineers, automotive safety leads, biotech researchers, financial quants, and the academics who will become tomorrow’s enterprise buyers. Every one of them needs a different page, and that has always been the part no marketing team could staff.

Now you can actually do it. Same team, same quarter, and none of it involves a design ticket or a content brief.

problemLanes.Need: Straight from your CRM, or whatever source you prefer
problemLanes.Outcome: Enterprise targets across automotive, aerospace, biotech, financial services, and the other industries you actively pursue. Named contacts in open deals. Name your personas once. That is the whole brief.

problemLanes.Need: Every source you connect, every account on the list
problemLanes.Outcome: Their site, their announcements, their procurement context, your CRM history, your open deals, and the outcomes you delivered for engineering teams that look just like them. Then the agents work out what matters to this one, today.

problemLanes.Need: Your brand, your domain, a live URL
problemLanes.Outcome: Written and designed inside your guidelines and published to your subdomain, ready for a seller or industry marketing manager to send. Auto-publish the ones you trust, hold review on the ones you don’t. Your call, set per programme.

A prospect announces a new simulation programme and the page picks it up. The deal moves stage and the page moves with it. No refresh project, no quarterly content audit, no Slack message to someone with a backlog.

faqs.Question: Which signals do you use?
faqs.Answer: Pick the ones you want analyzed, or let the agents surface the ones that matter to your buyer. There is no fixed list. If it lives in a system with an API, it is a variable.

faqs.Question: How do you handle 17 different industry audiences?
faqs.Answer: The same way the session works: you name the industry and the persona once, and the agents work out what actually matters to that buyer in that vertical. No separate briefing for each segment.

faqs.Question: Where does the copy come from?
faqs.Answer: Only from sources you approve: your site, your CRM, public filings, and news. Nothing is invented, and every block traces back to the signal behind it.

faqs.Question: Can we suppress technical product detail for non-technical buyers?
faqs.Answer: Yes. The same signal can appear on one page and be suppressed on another. You decide what is visible per programme, and the rule is set before anything publishes.

faqs.Question: Do we have to move our website?
faqs.Answer: No. Pages publish on a subdomain in your brand, so your current site stays exactly as it is.

faqs.Question: Who wrote this page?
faqs.Answer: An agent did, from public signals and the same brand rules the workshop uses. That is Limitless. Connect your own systems and the pages get considerably sharper than this one.
